summary: Aermotor LS40 lookout built 1950 near Parishville, run part-time until 1970 or 1971, since removed; cabin kept at a DEC shop; site today undocumented.

facts.design: 80-foot Aermotor LS40 steel fire lookout tower
facts.status_note: Tower removed after the lookout closed in 1970 or 1971; the observer's cabin survives at a DEC shop.
facts.agency: New York State Conservation Department, later the Department of Environmental Conservation

events.note: Built by the Conservation Department as an 80-foot Aermotor LS40 steel tower; Bill Starr's list also gives 1950 as the opening year
Began lookout operations in 1951; the first season logged 3 fires and 588 visitors
Decommissioned at the end of the 1970 fire season per Bill Starr's list; Wikipedia gives the last season as 1971
Tower later removed; the state list shows it as removed as of March 2011; no removal date given
Observer's cabin moved to the DEC Trout Lake Shop, where Operations Unit personnel use it; no date given
Parts reused in two platform towers at Wilson Hill WMA (#1 and #2) per the Forest Fire Lookout Association list; no second source found; no date given

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Bill Starr's list says the tower was decommissioned at the end of the 1970 season; Wikipedia says operations ended after the 1971 season and the tower was later removed. The story reports both.
The state list gives 1950 as the opening year, while Wikipedia gives 1951 as the year lookout operations began. The story gives 1950 for construction and 1951 for the first season.
Wikipedia gives 1,427 feet and the state list gives 1,436 feet. The story uses the Wikipedia figure.

sources.title: Fire Towers Operated by the NYS-DEC (list by Bill Starr, status as of March 2011)

notes_for_editor: No source describes the summit today or public access, so access stays unknown. The Wilson Hill WMA reuse rests on the Forest Fire Lookout Association list alone; Wikipedia repeats it from one tower listing. The cabin claim is from Wikipedia's article text; its own footnote was not checked. Closure year conflicts (1970 vs 1971) and the elevation difference (1,427 vs 1,436 ft) are both reported in the story. The record's status 'gone' and the Wilson Hill links are supported.
